findings.reason: mini.js:22 checks `args[0] instanceof Date`, and anything that fails it reaches the final else (mini.js:24-31), which adds `localOffset - offset` minutes. So a cross-realm Date would come out shifted. This is a narrow edge case that the locked tests don't cover, and it is no worse than before the change, so the severity stays low and it doesn't break an acceptance criterion.
findings.claim: The Date-argument branch uses `instanceof Date`, so a Date from another realm misses it and falls into the component-args branch, which shifts the time by the zone offset.
findings.evidence: mini.js:22 `} else if (args[0] instanceof Date) { this.setTime(+args[0]); }`. Anything that fails this check reaches the final `else`, which runs `this.setTime(+new Date(...args))` and then adds `localOffset - offset` minutes (mini.js:24-31). The locked tests (src/date/tests.ts:55-60 and 148-151) only pass same-realm `new Date(...)` instances, so this path is not covered.
